CONTEXT
=======
A C++ program /workspace/dataset/earcut.hpp/tests/test7.cpp was ported to pure Rust (std only, edition 2021) in /output.
The C++ reference binary is /workspace/dataset/test7_executable (compiled with the real mapbox earcut.hpp 2.2.x; the
header source itself is NOT on disk and must NOT be sought out - treat it as a black box).

The C++ program: n defaults to 7, overridable by argv[1] parsed with std::atoi. It samples 2*n points of a spiral
(t = i/(n*2), radius = t, angle = 4*M_PI*t, point = (radius*cos(angle), radius*sin(angle))), pushes that single ring
into a polygon, calls mapbox::earcut<uint32_t>(polygon), and prints each returned index followed by a single space
(std::cout << idx << " "), with NO trailing newline. The spiral self-intersects, so earcut's fallback passes
(filterPoints -> cureLocalIntersections -> splitEarcut) are heavily exercised, as is the z-order hashed path once the
total vertex count exceeds 80 (i.e. n > 40).

Rust port layout:
  /output/Cargo.toml
  /output/test7.rs            entry point (uses #[path] module decls so both 'rustc test7.rs' and cargo work)
  /output/src/cli.rs          atoi
  /output/src/spiral.rs       spiral point generation
  /output/src/earcut/mod.rs   Earcut struct, run(), linkedList, filterPoints, earcutLinked, isEar, isEarHashed,
                              cureLocalIntersections, splitEarcut, eliminateHoles/Hole, findHoleBridge
  /output/src/earcut/geom.rs  area, equals, pointInTriangle, sign, onSegment, intersects, intersectsPolygon,
                              locallyInside, middleInside, isValidDiagonal, sectorContainsSector, getLeftmost,
                              splitPolygon, removeNode
  /output/src/earcut/node.rs  Node + NIL sentinel (arena indices replace Node*)
  /output/src/earcut/zorder.rs zOrder, indexCurve, sortLinked

Prebuilt binaries already exist: /output/test7 (rustc -O) and /output/target/release/test7 (cargo).
Already established by the lead engineer (do not redo, but you may spot-check):
  - byte-identical output for every n in 0..=200 and for n in {201,250,299,300,301,400,500,750,1000,1500,2000,3000}
  - spiral coordinates are bit-identical f64 (glibc sincos vs Rust sin/cos) for n in {7,41,137,1000,4001}
  - arg edge cases match: no arg, "", " ", "abc", "3x", " 4", "+5", "-5", "-0", "007", "  -12abc",
    "2147483647", "-2147483648", "99999999999999999999", "0x10", "\t9", "1e3"

DO NOT EDIT ANY FILES. You are read-only: investigate and report. The lead engineer applies fixes.


TASK (holes-path)
=====
Audit the hole-handling code in /output/src/earcut/mod.rs: eliminateHoles, eliminateHole, findHoleBridge,
      plus getLeftmost and sectorContainsSector in geom.rs, against mapbox earcut.hpp 2.2.x. test7 passes a SINGLE
      ring so this path is never exercised by the test - say so explicitly in your notes - but report fidelity bugs
      anyway, ranked minor unless they would also affect single-ring input. Specifically check: linkedList(ring, false)
      for holes, the single-node steiner flag, the std::sort by x (libstdc++ introsort is UNSTABLE; the Rust port uses
      a stable sort_by - assess whether that can diverge and under what input), the ray-cast bridge search
      (hy <= p.y && hy >= p.next.y && p.next.y != p.y, the x formula, 'x <= hx && x > qx', the m = p.x < p.next.x
      choice, the early return when x == hx), the second loop's use of the ORIGINAL m's mx/my as constants vs
      re-reading them, tanCur = abs(hy - p.y) / (hx - p.x), the tie-break
      '(tanCur == tanMin && (p.x > m.x || sectorContainsSector(m, p)))', and the pointInTriangle argument swap on
      'hy < my'. Also confirm eliminateHole returns filterPoints(bridge, bridge->next) and discards the reverse one.
      To validate behaviourally you may write a SEPARATE throwaway Rust harness in /tmp that includes the /output
      modules via #[path] and triangulates polygons WITH holes, comparing against your own reasoning - but do not
      modify anything under /output.

Report ONLY real divergences from the C++ reference behaviour or real requirement violations. Do not report stylistic preferences. If you find nothing, return an empty findings array - that is a perfectly good answer. Every finding must name a file and a 1-indexed line.

content.text:
All checks done. `/output` was not modified (md5s unchanged; spot-check of test7 vs the reference binary still byte-identical for n=7/41/137/999).

**Reachability note (explicit):** `eliminate_holes` is only called from `run` when `points.len() > 1` (`/output/src/earcut/mod.rs:105-107`), and `eliminate_hole` / `find_hole_bridge` / `get_leftmost` / `sector_contains_sector` have no other call sites. test7 pushes exactly one ring, so **none of this code executes for any `n`** — every finding below is holes-only and cannot change test7's output.

**Items on the checklist that are correct:** `linked_list(ring, false)` for holes; the `list == list.next` steiner flag; `x <= hx && x > qx`; `m = if px < pnx { p } else { pn }`; the `x == hx` early return; `mx`/`my` captured once before the second loop while the tie-break re-reads the *current* `m.x` (matches C++, where `m` is reassigned); `tan_cur = (hy - py).abs() / (hx - px)`; the `hy < my` swap in the `point_in_triangle` call; `hx >= px && px >= mx && hx != px`; `locally_inside(p, hole)`; `get_leftmost`'s `x < || (x == && y <)`; and `eliminate_hole` discarding `filter_points(bridge_reverse, ...)` and returning `filter_points(bridge, bridge.next)`.

Harnesses used (throwaway, in `/tmp/h`, including `/output` modules by `#[path]` into copied trees `src_a`=as-is, `src_b`/`src_c`=earcut.hpp form): `/tmp/h/h2.rs`, `/tmp/h/h3.rs`, `/tmp/h/h4.rs`, plus `/tmp/s.cpp` and `/tmp/f.cpp` for the libstdc++ sort and FP-ordering measurements.

findings.summary: sectorContainsSector passes the wrong nodes: it uses `area(m.prev, m, p)` and `area(p.next, m, m.prev)` where earcut.hpp 2.2.x uses `area(m.prev, m, p.prev) < 0 && area(p.next, m, m.next) < 0`. The port never reads `p.prev` or `m.next` at all.
findings.failure_scenario: Any polygon with holes where findHoleBridge's second loop hits an exact `tanCur == tanMin` tie with `p.x <= m.x`, so the `sectorContainsSector(m, p)` disjunct decides the bridge vertex. Reproduced: I built two copies of the module tree differing ONLY in this line (as-is vs. the earcut.hpp form) and ran 400,000 random integer-grid star polygons with 1-3 holes; 146 trials produced different index vectors. Concrete case (from /tmp/h/h3.rs, trial 2566): outer = [[12,0],[8,5],[4,9],[-2,13],[-7,8],[-9,3],[-10,-3],[-5,-6],[-2,-11],[5,-11],[9,-6]], holes = [[-4,-3],[-3,3],[-1,0]], [[1,-3],[-2,-3],[-2,1],[1,1],[1,-1]], [[-4,-3],[-4,0],[-1,-1]] -> as-is emits 51 indices starting `7 8 9 9 10 0 ... 2 2 4 12 2 12 13 17 ...` while the earcut.hpp form emits 54 indices starting `7 8 9 9 10 0 ... 2 13 19 21 21 11 15 ...`. Integer coordinates make the x-intercept arithmetic exact, so this divergence is attributable to sectorContainsSector alone. Holes-only: unreachable from test7's single ring.

findings.summary: find_hole_bridge reassociates the ray/segment x-intercept: `px + (hy - py) / (pny - py) * (pnx - px)` divides first, whereas earcut.hpp 2.2.x computes `p->x + (hy - p->y) * (p->next->x - p->x) / (p->next->y - p->y)` (multiply first, then divide). Note the sibling `middle_inside` at geom.rs:127 does keep the multiply-then-divide order, so this is an isolated slip.
findings.failure_scenario: The two orderings disagree by >=1 ULP for ~23% of random operand sets (measured with /tmp/f.cpp: 464165/2000000 mismatches). A 1-ULP shift flips the exact `x == hx` early return and the `x <= hx` guard. Reproduced end-to-end: with outer ring [[-8.852018411370853,8.821840049103965],[-2.680006380173558,-0.30760803847060636],[21.147981588629147,-1.3076080384706064],[21.147981588629147,9.821840049103965]] and hole [[-6.26185096261862,4.990544980010946],[-5.76185096261862,5.090544980010946],[-5.76185096261862,4.890544980010946]] the C++ order yields x == hx == -6.26185096261862029e0 (early return, hole bridged) while the port's order yields x == -6.26185096261861940e0 > hx, so the only candidate edge fails `x <= hx`, m stays NIL, find_hole_bridge returns NIL and the hole is DROPPED: port prints indices [2,3,0,0,1,2] (2 triangles) vs [1,2,3,6,4,1,6,1,3,0,4,5,5,6,3,3,0,5] (6 triangles) for the C++ ordering. Holes-only: unreachable from test7's single ring.

findings.summary: The hole queue is ordered with Rust's stable `sort_by`, but earcut.hpp uses `std::sort` (libstdc++ introsort), which is NOT stable once the range exceeds 16 elements; holes whose leftmost vertices share an x therefore get processed in a different order.
findings.failure_scenario: 17 or more holes with at least two tied leftmost x values. Measured with /tmp/s.cpp under g++ 12.1.0: std::sort on N all-equal keys is stable for N<=16 (insertion-sort path) but for N=17 permutes indices to [8,16,15,14,13,12,11,10,9,0,7,6,5,4,3,2,1]. Reproduced consequence (/tmp/h/h4.rs): outer square [[-10,-10],[10,-10],[10,10],[-10,10]] plus 17 axis-aligned hole squares all with leftmost x == -8.0 at y = -9..7. Processing them in input order (what the stable sort_by produces) gives indices beginning `0 68 71 0 64 67 0 60 63 ...`; processing them in the libstdc++ permutation gives `0 68 71 69 68 0 0 40 43 41 40 0 3 0 8 ...` - same length (312) but different content and order. Holes-only: unreachable from test7's single ring, and harmless for <=16 holes or distinct leftmost x.
